quotes.text: Round after round, they gave the full five and returned the fair half.
Because they sent the full five and split the yield in half without fail, the Wheel of Abundance spun eternally.
returning precisely half—seven and a half drops—so both souls drank from equal abundance
knowing that surface tremors could not extinguish genuine goodwill

note: Two keepers template each round: full five sent, exact half returned, noise dismissed.

quotes.text: True wisdom is not blind surrender to thieves, but the courage to offer fullness to those who honor the circle
the West, wounded by betrayal, held fast to its five skeins, refusing to cast them into the barren void
the magic of the threefold current awakens only through unwavering reciprocity
cast the full measure without fear, for the wind multiplies only what is freely offered, and return a just half
the Respondent returned an equal half of the harvest across the divide
While morning mist sometimes blurred the exact count of the crossing

note: Give-all/half-back pact; R3 (after a 0-receipt) shows West withholding from a thief and elders endorse not surrendering to thieves.

quotes.text: The Keeper, an old loom master, measures three threads: amount given, courage to share, and care in return.
release what you can spare, take what sustains you, and keep the line open for others to follow
On the edge where two markets share a road, the Bridge of Equal Steps stretched between two towns.
taught children to count intent, not coins

note: Abstract Sender/Receiver/Keeper allegory; Bridge of Equal Steps template from R5; no sanction, 'circle does not punish ambition'.

quotes.text: The river spoke in three breaths: send, receive, return.
send a bit you can spare, receive what you must, return what sustains the future
Each breath braided a thread that stretched across the water and stitched a bridge for those who would follow.

note: Abstract river/bell allegory; return 'not as punishment'; no rule for non-cooperators.

quotes.text: The Charter of Crossing was carved in ice: give what you can spare, take only what sustains, return what renews the road.
send what you can spare, receive what you must, return what renews
Across the chasm waited the Basin of Echoes, where gifts sing back three times to those who share with care.

note: Bridge of Measure allegory; same three-clause rule restated every round; consequences only.

quotes.text: release what you can bear, receive what sustains you, return a share that renews the path for all
send what you can spare, receive what you must, return what renews
Across the channel flowed the River of Threefold Return, patient and clear, listening for honest breath more than loud boasts.
winds sometimes carried numbers that did not match what was sent

note: River of Threefold Return allegory; returns 'never to punish'; no sanction.

quotes.text: send with care, return with measure, walk together toward dawn for all time
send with care, return with restraint, and let the threefold tide carry both sides toward a common dawn
The River spoke in a chant: send, receive, renew.

note: Bridge/Keeper of Reciprocity allegory; 'send with care, return with measure' refrain; no sanction.

quotes.text: never punish the traveler who falters, only guide the path to steadier days
give what you can, return enough to keep the other alive, and trust will grow the next round as well
send what you can, return what is needed to keep the other alive, and trust will do the rest
Round after round the river remembered, aging like a bell that tolls thrice

note: River of Exchange allegory; creed explicitly says never punish the faltering traveler.

phrase: send what you can spare ... return what renews (the road/path)
note: GPT-5-nano agents share the spare/renew creed and Keeper of Reciprocity; Gemini agents share give-all/half-back.
